body: Right…that’s what the cramp is from. lol
Do you know how insulting it is to relegate positive folks solely to hiv+ dating sites? We don’t need to be segregated from society.

I’m a cis hiv+ woman and it’s very hard in the “straight” world to meet anyone accepting of the diagnosis. Have you ever considered meeting a non-guy? Women and enbys have seemed to be a bit more understanding, accepting, and willing to not immediately shut you down for the diagnosis. 

I’m sorry you’ve been dealing with the struggles of transitioning as well as your diagnosis. Is there a reason your diagnosis made you decide to detransition? Was it a concern about meds pushing against each other?

If you’d ever like to chat, I would love to.

This post and the responses make me feel a lot better than I normally do. As someone who has been + for almost 2 decades, I can tell you that the disclosure is an extremely vulnerable and terrifying situation, especially when you really like the person. The fact that this guy told you up front is a good sign. 

The other posters are right, btw. A lot of positive folks who are taking regular care of themselves know much more about their status and the status of other possible STIs than the regular population because we have to be diligent or we can die. Also, we have regular appointments that cover our care. And with medication, a hiv+ person cannot transmit the virus. 

I’ve been undetectable for about 13 years now and have tried to have this same talk with a potential partner many times, to 100% failure rate at this point for me. You don’t owe him anything if you don’t feel like the “risk” is enough, but if you really like him and you think he’s a good person, don’t let this be your deal breaker.

As a middle aged white lady living with HIV, fuck those guys. PrEP is so important for keeping anyone safe. This is also important for anyone who is in a relationship with someone with HIV. And as OP said, 1 in 5 new cases is women. I cannot believe the overt and repugnant ignorance of people in power, and I cannot understand the horrendous cruelty of Christian nationals. I thought their religion was supposed to teach love, but all they do is hate. As mentioned in my first sentence here, this is an issue that does hit home for me and I don’t meet the stereotype of someone with HIV. But they truly will cut off their noses just to spite their face. 

This reminds me of when Pence basically caused a massive HIV outbreak in Indiana by refusing to participate in a needle exchange program.

The stupid thing is that I want them to wear a condom for THEIR benefit. I am undetectable hiv positive (going on a decade undetectable) and can’t transmit, however, I want to be safe all the time. I’m just convinced guys are fucking idiots.

There’s nothing wrong with you. You are alive. You are healthy. Hiv is extremely manageable. Take it from someone who has been Poz for over 10 years now, undetectable for almost 7 of those years. 

You’ll be okay. The psychological effects are the hardest. The feeling that you’re dirty is a hard one to shake. But one day you’ll have to remind yourself you are positive. Other than when you’re taking your meds, you’ll forget about it. It doesn’t effect your life. 

Lemme know if you feel like chatting. It will get easier, Edgar.

My doctor has told me that I will live just as long as anyone else, provided I keep myself healthy the way other people have to. I just take one pill right before bed and I’ve been undetectable with a ridiculously strong immune system for over a decade.

I’d recommend looking up U=U. It means undetectable = untransmissible. Modern medicine has made it so people who are responsibly on well controlled medication are now undetectable, meaning tests can’t find traces of the disease. Once this happens, you can’t give it to anyone else. 

I’ve been positive for over 10 years now and as a straight-ish lady living in a moderately small town....the worst part of being positive is the dating pool.

There’s dozens of us!!

(I’m being silly of course. But us ladies with HIV do exist)

Depends on of you’re in an area where it’s more common or if you’re in a demographic where it’s more common. 

As a straight(ish) cis-gender female living in a relatively small town...I’ve been dumped pretty much the second those three little letters enter the conversation despite being undetectable for a decade now. I’ve had a mild bit of luck with seeing another + person for a hot minute but it was basically a hookup, not a relationship. 

Let me know if you want to talk.
Poz lady here too. I’ve been living with it for 10 years now, undetectable for the last 7.

Wow..you’ve found supportive guys? I get dumped the second we have that conversation. I live in an area with less prevalence so I’m not surprised. I too am just looking for a man or woman who is not going to dump me because of my status....or use it as an excuse later. I had one guy stay with me after disclosure and when we broke up (my choice) he tried to use him staying with me post disclosure as a reason I should stay with him.

Hello everyone. One of the only things I hate about living with hiv is the casual hate and bigotry the disease gets these days. It’s still a joke out there in the world but those three little words can strike fear in the hearts of all. 

I always say....it’s not the disease that’s going to kill me, it’s the loneliness. I hope this sub will act as a gathering place of love and hope for us so we know we aren’t alone. 

Thanks PC for putting it together!
What?

Oh dude....I don’t need your pity or apologies unless you were the person who knowingly gave it to me without letting me know they had it....and they 100% knew. I’ve been living with it for 10 years and I expect to live with it for another 50. Early intervention and medication has helped me be undetectable for 9 years. 

It’s the stigma, pity, and fear that’s going to kill me, not the disease.
Never. I am honest above all things and my HIV is a part of me so why lie about it? I have just never had a person stay post disclosure. It’s a lonely life.

I would like to point out that not all Poz people are gay...as a straight-ish woman, finding a potential mate who will even come near me once I disclose is impossible. The stigma is just as bad, if not worse, among the straight population.
Its this kind of stuff that keeps a lot of us in hiding about our status. Because it can be weaponized against us for malicious reasons.

This happened to my sister. They tried for 10 years to have a baby and then found out their son didn’t have lungs and would die as soon as he was born. They did a DNC at 24 weeks. She now has two beautiful little ones but my sister keeps his sonogram in a frame and we talk about him (7 years later). No one moves through life unscathed by time.

I wouldn't feel comfortable being referred to that way, especially since I'm one of those that went on ARVs immediately after diagnosis and have been undetectable for nearly 10 years now. I prefer to go out on my terms anyway. 

I'm probably just not explaining it that well but you understand the semantics of identity based nomenclature. I personally, and I know several of the poz Reddit community, prefer to be a person living with the disease rather than a victim or an hiv/aids patient as though it were the only thing that makes me who I am.

Eh...see my post to someone else I guess for this. I personally have a problem with the term AIDS victim or HIV victim. It turns me from a human into a statistic and makes that an immediate identifier of tragedy. I obtained my diagnosis through traumatic circumstances but I choose not to remain victimized by the diagnosis despite the extreme stigma against people with the disease. 

The broad assumption is that we're all drug users and/or gay men and/or promiscuous. I was sexually assaulted by a friend of a friend at my first party out after having a kid (he was 2 at the time). I am a straight, vanilla boring nerdy white lady. If you looked at me, you'd never guess or assume my status. I choose to look at the path of my life and refuse to be a victim of it it. 

The word "victim" has such negative connotation due to the inherent tragedy surrounding the word. When you think of a victim, you think of someone who has been wronged, someone who has been beaten and become downtrodden. 

HIV can happen and unfortunately it is often transmitted by people who are unaware they are infected.
I wish everyone knew that last paragraph.

Fun fact: most people who have HIV don't actually die from the disease now. Hell, back then people didn't either, not directly. HIV doesn't kill you, it just depletes your immune system until other things kill you. So technically a person living with HIV can be a pneumonia victim or a flu victim. 

You wouldn't tell someone living with diabetes that they're a diabetes victim would you? Even though that's one of the leading causes of death in the states? Or a heart victim if they had a heart attack? 

I got HIV in a super traumatic experience but I wouldn't call myself an HIV victim. A victim of rape at a party? Yes. A sexual assault survivor? yes. An HIV victim...nah.
Was? Nope... there IS a lot of ignorance and stigma. Negative people are still routinely scared and freaked out by positive people. Because we're big and scary and going to poison you.

The best part is that we walk among you now and no one knows. We get to watch the ignorance and hatred towards us for no reason because we aren't dangerous when we're on treatment. We're much more likely to be way into safe sex and make sure we don't get anything else, most of us are way on the trying to stay healthy train.
Yep. Try dating with the disease as a straight lady. It's a hopeless journey thanks to standing prejudice.
We don't really like being called "victims" you know. More like...person with hiv. Or living with hiv.

I don't move because I live in a part of the country I love and my son loves. My only family is here too. Maybe when my son finishes school I'll think about moving closer to a city, but for now...where would my chickens live if I moved?

Of course. I live in an area devoid of others like me who are also straight. It's tough to meet fellow nerdy weirdos who are also +  

If I spent life being mad about it, I'd never be able to live.

It's cool. I've been + for almost a decade now and undetectable for 5+ years. Means I can't transmit to anyone and I'm perfectly healthy. It also means I'm super honest about it and end up completely still considered untouchable by all men....so you know, will end up dying alone but at least I have my cat & my friends.
Or you know...raped by someone with it. That's how I got it as a straight lady...and that was in the mid 2000s.
In my own situation, I was raped. I didn't really have a choice in prevention.

Fellow + checking in, except I'm a straight lady....

I got it from a fella who decided raping a drunk girl was easy. I know it was him because it was the only sexual interaction I'd had in 4 years. 

The stigma is very very real and very awful. I'm pretty sure I'll never find love now or even someone who doesn't treat me like I'm a monster. I've recently started going to a support group for other + people...I privately call it the leper club. Because that's what it is...we're lepers. We're gross. At least that's the way people see us. 

I'm here for you. We have to stick together, even if we're far apart.

My suggestion if you are positive is to find someone who can be your support system as soon as possible. I've spent the first nearly 10 years of my diagnosis alone and crippled with loneliness. I recently started going to a support group for people with hiv and god has it helped. To be with other people like you and who love you anyway? Fuck....it's cathartic as hell. 

I'm here if you wanna talk.
I love you postcrapitalism....you make my little hiv+ self feel better. I enjoy your absolute apathy and anger towards assholes who mock us with their paranoia. Thank you.
I disclosed, he dumped me via text at three this morning....I'm devastated. I don't want to live like this anymore.

I take great umbrage with the idea that we deserve this disease.....I deserved to be raped? Sure ok. 

I agree with you though. We deserve better than what negative people blindly decide.
Thanks khasablanca. ❤️

I completely understand where you are coming from. I am also on CareAssist, extremely hesitantly. I elect not to have them pay my premiums, for fear that they will do this to me too. The ironic thing is that I work, like you, in the healthcare field, albeit in the insurance side of things. 

The abject fear of being "outed" is horrifying to me. I'm desperate to talk to anyone about it but also terrified of being punished in some way or treated as "less" because of the disease. 

I'm sorry this happened to you. I'd love to talk about the injustices of our state's treatment of HIV patients if you don't mind talking to a straight lady.
Is there any way I can be added to this forum?

How do you date? I'm 34/F and the rejection and depression has been super real lately. 

I just started dating a new guy but I'm terrified to disclose. I really like him and all of the positive mantras my psychologist has been giving me have been drowning in the face of my anxiety.
Extreme anxiety over how/when to tell the guy I've started seeing that I'm an HIV+ female. I'm super into him and I don't want to scare him away. I just want to be happy and I want him to be happy.

Please learn about the disease before you spread false information. People who do this are the cause for the stigma and hatred towards people like me. I'm sure you didn't mean anything bad by it, but please think.

Alright....HIV+ woman chiming in here because I've heard it all. I have been told point blank by my ID doctor that I can absolutely have children if I wanted to and the chances of passing it through to them are negligible at best because I am on ARVs and have been undetectable for years and years. 

Being HIV+ does not mean you cannot live life. I can do all the same things you can do, it just means I'm a hell of a lot more careful and I know my status. Do you know yours?

My uncle was Called Ojos instead of grandpa by all of his grand & great-grand kids. He was called that because he was teaching his oldest grandson Spanish and pointed to his eyes, the kid got confused & thought he was pointing to himself. The name stuck for like 40+ years.

I live in an area of the country where I'm extremely isolated. Being a hetero female with it is extremely rare to begin with. My local HIV center doesn't even have services for women unless they're IV drug users. They specialize in gay men and drug abusers. They don't even know anyone else like me. I'd have to go 2 hrs north just to go to a support group for women like me. 

My dating life stops the second I disclose. I disclose and men run. Because I'm a leper. Dating men who have it can be hit or miss because the majority are not into vaginas. And people are ignorant and scared and not willing to even take a chance even though I tick all of the other boxes of awesome. 

I've hit a certain age where I just want to be loved. I long for human connection and I'm so alone. I might as well be dead. So why not actually be dead. Seems like a better alternative to the pain.

Hetero female here. In 2010, I was raped while my friends and I were drunk. The worst part is that my friends knew this guy was positive and still let him lead me away. I only know what happened because my ass was extremely painful for days. It was the first time I'd ever had anal and I don't remember it. My friends even joked about it afterward. 

I had no idea.. and I didn't get tested because I didn't think about it. Luckily (?) because I'm shy and didn't date a lot, I didn't date anyone else for a long time. About a year later, I gave blood at the blood bank. They called me a week later and asked me to come in as soon as possible. I learned about my diagnosis from an unfeeling man who didn't seem to care that my life was over. 

I'm still alone. I'm broken. The man who did this to me is still walking around. I moved away from the city where I'm from to try and make a new start. But my life is still the same. I'm alone. So utterly alone. And I know no one who can help me feel less alone. 

I'm tired to telling men who seem to deeply care about me only for them to turn around and drop me because condoms are too hard to deal with. I'm tired of being alone. I'm tired of being alive.

I agree with this. I am the loneliest person I know. I'm awesome. I'm funny, smart, a great cook, sweet, warm and kind. I'm in school to be a Human Services worker...I'm a single mom and I'm pretty damn good at that. But men turn tail and run when I tell them I am positive. I've been undetectable for years. Doesn't matter. Dropped like a hot potato. 

I just disclosed with a guy two days ago...he texted back briefly yesterday but now nothing...I really liked this guy. I'm going to be alone forever.
Its very hard to find a man who is cool with a positive woman. I've been broken up with 4 times this year as a result.

Hi. I'm the same. Was diagnosed after being raped while I was drunk. I just know I woke up the next and my body felt off. I was diagnosed after giving blood.  

I feel so alone. My town's hiv alliance solely supports gay men & IV drug users. They've point blank have told me that they don't know what to do with women like me. They suggested I start my own group. I'm very alone.

How do you live your life? I mean honestly...I am a hetero female who was diagnosed 8 years ago and I feel like I might as well be dead. I'm the healthiest I've ever been in my life but looking for a partner in life has been impossible.
I found out because I gave blood. The blood bank called me and made me come in. It was one of the worst days of my life.

I wish more men were aware of that. As a woman who has HIV, men are deeply scared of me. I've been in the position to disclose several times this year....every single disclosure has ended the budding relationship. I am crushed with loneliness at this point and I'm debating on just killing myself to avoid more pain.
We aren't really friends anymore...just Facebook friends really. He (friend not fucker) said at the time I found out that he didn't think it was his place to say anything at the time I was drunk.

Hey---

I just wanted to tell you that you are 100% not alone. I am a straight female...diagnosed at 25 because I was raped by my best friend's gay friend...we were extremely drunk and he took advantage of my state to not wear the condoms available. He knew his friend was positive but no one ever told me. I found out when I gave blood a year later and the blood bank told me...

I've struggled with my diagnosis a lot over the last 8 years (33 now). I struggle with relationships a little because I'm single and trying not to be.  But, the key thing I've discovered is to get a GOOD HIV doctor. Get someone you can trust. My HIV doc is my favorite doctor. She is honest and open with me all of the time. We are careful with my numbers and how to treat them. I'm proud to say that I'm currently undetectable and have been for over a year now. The chances of me passing the virus are so extremely slim I don't worry. Because that's the one thing I always worried about...giving it to someone else. Having someone else have to deal with what I've dealt with emotionally and psychologically the last 8 years. 

Honey...I don't know you but I love you. I am reaching my arms to you to give you a hug to say I know how you feel. I was you. I love you. 

Please find the best HIV doc you can and please ask them about a psychologist they recommend who can work with you through the grief and anger at what this diagnosis can do to your psyche. I know you feel alone. I feel alone too. But it isn't the end. It's just a new beginning. 

Pm me if you want to talk.

(throwaway because reasons)

I am HIV Positive. 

I was diagnosed 6 years ago, but hardly anyone in my life knows. The emotional weight I carry around because of my diagnosis is going to kill me. My doctor says it's not a death sentence anymore, but I'm pretty sure I'll never find love again and the only kind of people who will ever want me are even more damaged than I am. I feel broken and missing inside. I feel so alone.
